before.stem: What assumption is hidden when WordNetLemmatizer.lemmatize(word) is called without a POS argument?
before.subtopic: NLTK preprocessing code and intermediate state
assumptions: Supplemental premise: the inspected NLTK 3.10.3 signature defaults pos to n; no automatic sentence tagging is performed by this isolated call.

options.text: It first calls the sentence POS tagger and uses all predicted tags automatically
It always treats every token as a verb
It inherits the grammatical tag returned by any earlier pos_tag call, even when that tag is not passed to lemmatize.
It uses the default noun POS rather than inferring every word’s grammatical role from the sentence

citations.locator: Printed slide 10: Step 5 default lemmatize(word) call
citations.evidenceText:
import nltk
import string
from nltk.tokenize import word_tokenize
from nltk.corpus import stopwords
from nltk.stem import WordNetLemmatizer
text = "Pick up the red ball near the chair!"
# Step 1: Convert to lowercase
text = text.lower()
# Step 2: Remove punctuation
text = text.translate(str.maketrans('', '', string.punctuation))
# Step 3: Tokenization
tokens = word_tokenize(text)
# Step 4: Remove stopwords
stop_words = set(stopwords.words('english'))
filtered_tokens = [
    word for word in tokens
    if word not in stop_words]
# Step 5: Lemmatization
lemmatizer = WordNetLemmatizer()
lemmatized_tokens = [
    lemmatizer.lemmatize(word)
    for word in filtered_tokens]

citations.locator: Printed slide 29: Main definition and explanatory bullets
citations.evidenceText:
Transformers
•  Using attention mechanism, transformers can learn:
    – Which words are important
    – Which words are related
    – Where the model should focus
•   In the command C1, the robot must focus on:
    – “move” : the action
    –  “robot” : object to be moved
    –  “shelf” : spatial context
•  This helps the model to connect related words, track
   context and understand references and relationships
• When transformer models were trained on massive
  amounts of text and scaled to billions of parameters, they
   evolved into Large Language Models (LLMs).
